description: We are a team of five Computer Science students from UET Lahore and Arid Agriculture University Rawalpindi: Subhan, Zakaullah, Muhammad Abrar, Maaz Ur Rehman and Ahsan Ali. Our interests include AI/ML, software development, data analysis, and space exploration. We aim to build AeroFlame Intelligence, an evidence-based platform exploring NASA's microgravity combustion data. We welcome collaboration in Python, AI, web development, data visualization, design, and space science.
summary:
AeroGuard AI is an evidence-grounded research intelligence platform designed to help researchers and space-safety teams explore NASA's microgravity combustion research. It brings together NASA research records and BASS-II experimental data in one interactive dashboard, allowing users to search studies, compare findings, explore experimental conditions, and generate structured research insights.

The platform uses a local-first research retrieval system with NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS) search as an additional source when local evidence is insufficient. It distinguishes experimental findings, simulations, interpretations, and unverified information, while preserving source references and scientific limitations.

AeroGuard AI aims to make decades of space-combustion research easier to discover and interpret, supporting better-informed research into spacecraft fire safety for future missions. It is a research-support prototype, not a certified fire-detection or suppression system.
details:
AeroGuard AI is an interactive research intelligence dashboard developed to make NASA microgravity combustion and spacecraft fire-safety research more accessible, searchable, and interpretable.

The platform includes six main areas:

  1. Dashboard Overview: Provides an overview of the research collection and available capabilities.
  2. NASA Research Search: Searches stored research passages and can retrieve additional NASA NTRS catalogue records when local evidence is insufficient.
  3. BASS-II Data: Allows users to explore and search experimental records from the Burning and Suppression of Solids-II investigation.
  4. Research Insights: Organizes research findings into structured, evidence-linked insights.
  5. Research Comparison: Helps compare findings across studies while preserving differences in experimental conditions.
  6. Mission Intelligence: Generates structured research briefs relevant to spacecraft fire-safety questions.

The backend is built with Python and FastAPI. The frontend uses React, TypeScript, Vite, and Recharts. Research data is stored locally in structured JSON files, with SQLite used for review records.

A key design principle is scientific traceability. The system preserves source identifiers, document references, page information, and evidence categories. Experimental observations are not treated as interchangeable with simulations or interpretations. Automated scores are not presented as scientific validation.

The project is designed as a research-support prototype. It does not certify materials, predict every fire scenario, or replace NASA safety procedures or expert judgment.

Our goal is to help researchers explore existing evidence more efficiently and support future research into safer human space exploration.
